h1: The 6 Best FlexiSpot Standing Desk Converters of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six FlexiSpot standing desk converters, electric and gas-spring, from 36 to 42 inches, compared on width, lift type and price.
summary: The FlexiSpot 36 inch electric converter is the best pick for most desks because it adds a motor without moving out of the $100 to $200 tier. The 42 inch and 40 inch electric models cost more and add width. The three manual gas spring risers suit buyers who want no cord and stand only occasionally.
intro: Most buyers assume a motor means a big jump in price. In FlexiSpot's converter range, that assumption is wrong at the small end: a 36 inch electric riser sits in the same price tier as manual gas spring models, so defaulting to the spring version can mean skipping a feature you could easily afford.

We ranked six FlexiSpot converters on platform width, lift type and price tier. Two other models were left out, one with no listed price and one with a thin spec line. Every claim below comes from the listings, so we avoid inventing details about weight capacity or lift range.

products.name: FLEXISPOT 36 Inch Electric Standing Desk Converter, Motorized Sit to Stand Riser
products.verdict: An electric lift with a 36 inch platform at the lower price tier.
products.description:
This FlexiSpot is a 36 inch electric sit to stand converter with a motorized lift and push button height changes, listed in the $100 to $200 tier. It is the narrowest of the electric models, which suits standard desks that carry a laptop and one monitor.

It wins because it brings a motor into the cheaper price tier, where the gas spring risers also sit. The 42 inch and 40 inch electric models cost a tier more, and what they add is surface area rather than new functions. Against the manual 36 inch riser, there is no price penalty for the motor.

Buy it if you move between sitting and standing often and want effortless height changes. The caveats are a nearby outlet and a narrower surface than the 40 and 42 inch models.
products.idealFor: Standard desks that need a motor on a budget.

products.name: FLEXISPOT 42 Inch Electric Motor Desk Converter, Height Adjustable Motorized
products.verdict: The widest electric FlexiSpot here, in the $200-500 tier.
products.description:
The 42 inch electric FlexiSpot has a motorized lift and the widest platform among the electric models, and it falls in the $200 to $500 tier. That extra width gives room for two monitors, a laptop and a keyboard without crowding.

It takes second because the same motor costs a tier less in the 36 inch version. What you buy with the extra money is six inches of surface, and nothing else in the listing suggests more power. The 40 inch electric below it shares the price tier but offers less width, which is why it falls behind.

Choose it for dual screen or multi device desks. Skip it if 36 inches covers your gear. The caveat is that it needs a wide desk, and the larger footprint can overhang a narrow one.

products.name: FLEXISPOT 40 Inch Electric Standing Desk Converter, Height Adjustable Riser
products.verdict: A 40 inch electric converter between the 36 and 42.
products.description:
The 40 inch FlexiSpot is an electric height adjustable riser with a 40 inch platform, in the $200 to $500 tier. It sits between the 36 and 42 inch electric models on width.

It ranks third because it shares the 42 inch model's price tier while offering less surface, so the only reason to pick it is a desk that cannot fit 42 inches. Compared with the 36 inch electric, you gain four inches of room but pay a tier more.

Pick it when your desk is a few inches too narrow for the 42 inch version and the 36 inch feels cramped. Otherwise go smaller for savings or larger for space. It also needs an outlet within cable reach, which can be a problem on desks that sit away from the wall.

products.name: FLEXISPOT Standing Desk Converter 42 Inch, Extra Large Ergonomic Height Adjustable
products.verdict: A 42 inch gas-spring riser at the lower price tier.
products.description:
This 42 inch FlexiSpot is a manual converter with a gas spring lift, listed in the $100 to $200 tier. It gives the same 42 inch platform as the electric top-end model, without the motor or the power cord.

It ranks fourth because it delivers the width at the lower price, with the trade-off of lifting the surface by hand against the spring. Against the electric 36 inch, you gain six inches of space but give up push button convenience.

It suits wide desks where you stand now and then rather than all day. Skip it if you switch positions several times an hour, because the electric 36 inch will serve better and cost the same. The caveat is the large footprint, so measure your desk before ordering.

products.name: FLEXISPOT Standing Desk Converter 40 Inch Large Desk Riser, Spacious
products.verdict: A 40 inch gas-spring riser in the cheaper tier.
products.description:
The 40 inch manual FlexiSpot uses a gas spring lift and a 40 inch platform, and it sits in the $100 to $200 tier. No outlet is needed, which helps desks far from a socket.

It lands fifth because the 42 inch manual model offers more width for the same tier. Its case rests on desks where two inches matters, and on buyers who find 42 inches too bulky. Compared with the electric 36 inch, it gives more surface but no motor.

Buy it for a mid width desk at low cost if you are comfortable raising the platform by hand. The honest caveat is that it gives up the motor at a price where electric is available, so make sure you actually need the extra four inches.

products.name: FLEXISPOT Standing Desk Converter 36 Inch Desk Riser, Height Adjustable
products.verdict: A 36 inch gas-spring riser in the same tier as the electric 36.
products.description:
The 36 inch manual FlexiSpot is a gas spring riser listed in the $100 to $200 tier. It has no power cord and a 36 inch platform for a laptop and one screen.

It finishes last because the 36 inch electric model sits in the very same tier with a motor, which makes this one hard to justify. Its only real argument is a cordless setup where the nearest outlet is far from the desk.

Buy it if you want a simple spring lift and have no power at hand. Skip it in every other case, because the electric version above costs the same. The caveat is manual lifting, so keep the load on the surface light enough that you are happy to raise it several times a day.

whatMatters.detail: Lift type is the mechanism that raises the platform. Electric models move at the press of a button, while gas spring models rise by hand against a spring. It matters if you change position often. The listing title names electric or gas spring, so check that before comparing prices.

Platform width is the surface area in inches, and it sets how much gear fits. A 36 inch platform suits a laptop and one monitor, while 42 inches handles more screens. Compare the listed width with your desk's width and leave a small margin at each side.

Price tier is the bucket in which the listing sits, here running from $100 to $200 up to $200 to $500. It matters because a 36 inch electric costs the same tier as manual models. Read the bucket alongside the lift type, rather than assuming motors cost more.

Power needs differ by model. Electric converters require an outlet near the desk, while manual ones do not. It matters if your desk sits in the middle of a room or far from a socket. Trace the route of the cable before ordering an electric unit.

Desk depth is how much of your desk the converter uses. A riser takes up front to back space too, so a shallow desk may feel crowded. The listings give platform width in inches, so check the depth on the product page and compare it with your desk.

faq.q: Why are the 32 and 35 inch models missing?
faq.a: One lacked a listed price bucket and the other had a thin spec line, so we ranked six clearer listings instead. Everything here comes from the data on each page, including the 36, 40 and 42 inch widths.

Yes at 36 inches, because the electric FlexiSpot costs the same $100 to $200 tier as the manual risers. At 40 and 42 inches the electric models sit a tier higher, so the decision depends on how often you switch.
No. The manual 36, 40 and 42 inch models use a gas spring that you raise by hand. Only the electric FlexiSpot converters need an outlet close to the desk.
The 42 inch models give the most room, in either electric or manual form. The 42 inch electric is the better choice if you move often, and the 42 inch manual saves a tier of cost.

faq.q: Can I use a 36 inch riser on a small desk?
faq.a: Measure your desk depth and width first. The 36 inch electric or manual models suit smaller desks, but the listings only give platform width, so check depth on the product page too.
It is a spring assisted lift that you raise and lower by hand, with no motor. The three manual FlexiSpot models use this type, which keeps them cord free and a bit simpler.

finalTake: Start with the 36 inch electric model, since it costs no more than the manual versions. Step up to the 42 inch electric converter only if you run several screens, and choose a manual riser when the nearest outlet is out of reach or you stand rarely. The 36 inch manual is the hardest model to justify here.
